correctness.rationale: The norm of normalized convolution is the absolute kernel mean by taking the sign of the real kernel at the identity, and self-adjointness gives the L1 endpoint by duality. The same sign witness works over either scalar field. Adding an independent sign Y changes the cubic kernel from E3 to E3+Y E2, and the average of |E3+E2| and |E3-E2| is max(|E3|,|E2|). This gives the stated increment and the pointwise equality condition. Newton identities on signs give the displayed E2 and E3. For even n, s=0 witnesses strict increase; for odd n, the points |s|=1 contribute zero increment. At positive odd s>=3 the squared comparison factors with sign given by (s(s-2)-3n)(s(s+2)-3n). The corresponding open intervals exactly partition the interior of [3,n(n+2)] except their shared endpoints. This proves equality exactly at 3n=r(r+2) for odd r>=3: in the converse n=r(r+2)/3>=r+2 and n is odd, so both adjacent lattice points are available. Integrality is r congruent to 1 or 3 mod 6, giving the two families and count sqrt(X/3)+O(1). Read the frozen proof, verification notes and code without executing uploaded code. Direct sign enumeration for dimensions 3–8 and exact comparisons through n=300 were separately reproduced (including plateaus 225 and 261 above the frozen check range). evidence: The related exact binomial formula splits the signs of the kernel at 0 and plus or minus sqrt(3n-2) in each fixed dimension. Conditioning on the final sign instead tests the product (E3+E2)(E3-E2), i.e., pairs of neighboring next-dimension kernel signs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For odd n the noncentral next-dimension root, if it lands at the even site r+1, yields 3n+1=(r+1)^2. If it lies between even sites, the opposed pair contributes a strictly positive increment. The prior fixed-dimension formula and cubic-root equation provide ingredients, but neither mechanically identifies the no-opposed-pair criterion or its parity boundary. The substantive assertion is the exact bridge between the norm equality and the root location, not the elementary solution of the square equation.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The finite formula in the distinct result can reproduce any finite prefix; it is not an all-dimension classification of equality. For every odd n the plateau condition is equivalent to a noncentral even-lattice zero of the cubic kernel in dimension n+1, not to a zero in dimension n; the central zero in dimension n+1 alone cannot encode a plateau. Known root tables on their own lack the link to zero increments.

originality.rationale: The known norm identity, fixed-degree asymptotics and cubic Krawtchouk algebra are not new. The supported distinct claim is the exact one-step equality classification for the cubic endpoint norms and its positive-part formula. The strongest same-invariant comparisons give the exact per-dimension norm or its asymptotics, not the pointwise one-step comparison and infinite zero-increment set. An integer root in the next even dimension is another formulation of the new plateau criterion; the arithmetic of those roots is not a separately new claim.
residual_risks: No relevant open copy of Habsieger–Stanton was recovered; this is not evidence that the root arithmetic is new. A differently indexed equivalent consecutive-norm result remains possible. No precedence is inferred from dates shared by the two related indexed entries.

value.rationale: This classifies exactly when extending the ambient cube adds no endpoint norm, despite the strictly enlarged cubic span. It reveals a sparse but infinite parity-sensitive obstruction and gives a quantitative increment formula. One can use this exact comparison to distinguish finite-dimensional norm behavior that per-dimension leading asymptotics do not resolve.
